sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Funding for a 12-month Governance Incentives Framework R&D project to research, model, test, and propose governance incentive mechanisms for Cardano.

Deliverables: Governance Incentives Framework, public governance activity dataset, public website and dashboard, documented incentive models and formula outputs, controlled incentive pilot and findings report, at least one publication-ready research paper submitted for peer review, completed and submitted Governance Incentives Framework CIP, governance integration pathway and governance action to DReps, final financial and milestone report

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will deliver a Governance Incentives Framework, public dataset and dashboard, documented model outputs, research publications, controlled pilot findings, and a governance integration pathway over seven milestones in 12 months.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer states that a Governance Incentives Working Group mapping document identified 49 relevant efforts, proposals, research papers, tools, and initiatives related to Cardano governance incentives.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The proposal cites early governance data showing active DReps declined in every 12-epoch period, the DRep Gini coefficient increased from 0.92 to 0.94, and 11-16 DReps represent 51% of voting power.

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposer argues that without a structured incentive framework, Cardano risks making governance compensation decisions reactively, politically, or inconsistently.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will develop and simulate incentive models using governance activity data, community feedback, expert input, and prior reward-scheme research, evaluating participation, decentralization, concentration, accountability, gaming risk, and budget sustainability.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): A controlled incentive pilot will fund one clearly defined experiment, launch during the data-collection phase, and publish methodology, results, deviations, limitations, and implications.
missing: Independent evidence for: The proposer states that a Governance Incentives Working Group mapping document identified 49 relevant efforts, proposals, research papers, tools, and initiatives related to Cardano governance incentives.
Independent evidence for: The proposer argues that without a structured incentive framework, Cardano risks making governance compensation decisions reactively, politically, or inconsistently.

Independent evidence for: The team claims relevant Cardano governance, Catalyst, research, and blockchain experience, including successfully closed Catalyst proposals and Governance Incentives Working Group involvement.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unknown (stale snapshot) (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The project will deliver a Governance Incentives Framework, public dataset and dashboard, documented model outputs, research publications, controlled pilot findings, and a governance integration pathway over seven milestones in 12 months." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The proposer states that a Governance Incentives Working Group mapping document identified 49 relevant efforts, proposals, research papers, tools, and initiatives related to Cardano governance incentives." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
